proposals.warning: At the September activity report, check by **9 October 2026**, re-read if fully electronic US high-grade share is below **18.0%** or high-yield share below **7.5%**, against August's **19.0% and 8.3%**. At Q3 results, locally dated **29 October**, also warn if cash-credit fee per million falls more than **15% year on year**, or credit revenue stops growing despite rising credit volume. These are my decision thresholds, not management guidance. They test customer loss and weakening monetisation before total company earnings necessarily fall. [August baseline](https://www.tradeweb.com/newsroom/media-center/news-releases/tradeweb-reports-august-2026-total-trading-volume-of-%2461.2-trillion-and-average-daily-volume-of-%242.8-trillion), [quarterly fee disclosure](https://investors.tradeweb.com/static-files/e5696c92-ff61-4d32-85b0-678deedf8d9a).
proposals.break: Recommend exit under §5.1 if, in **each of Q3 and Q4 2026**, cash-credit fee per million falls more than **15% year on year and credit revenue declines**, even if trading volume or group profit rises. Independently, break if high-grade share is below **17.0%**, or high-yield below **7.0%**, in **three consecutive post-entry monthly disclosures**. Review these by **28 February 2027**, using earlier observations as they arrive. A lost customer franchise or persistently worse revenue economics can therefore fail the thesis without a group margin collapse. Missing or redefined disclosure is a review trigger, never an assumed pass.

proposals.warning: At FY2026 results, checked by **10 November 2026**, re-read upon any of: another disclosed decline in consolidated physical volumes; free cash flow at or below **70% of company-adjusted net income**; or **filed operating income / year-end total assets below 13.5%**. The cash threshold is management's commitment; the return threshold is my decision rule against a **14.17% FY2025 baseline**. Volumes come from the sales bridge, not a price-driven revenue percentage. No volume disclosure means unavailable evidence, not flat volume. [Q3 outlook](https://ir.muellerwaterproducts.com/press-releases/2026/08-05-2026-211118748), [annual operating income](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1350593/000135059325000066/R5.htm), [balance sheet](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1350593/000135059326000036/mwa-20260630.htm).
proposals.break: Recommend exit under §5.1 if FY2026 filed operating income / year-end total assets is **below 12%**, **or** FY2026 free cash flow is **below 50% of company-adjusted net income**. Check by **10 November 2026**, or immediately when the annual filing supplies the denominator. Independently, two successive September and December quarters with filed GAAP operating margin below **18% in each** break the case, checked by **28 February 2027**, whether or not reported volume also falls. These are my thresholds, not forecasts or management guidance. Define free cash flow as operating cash flow less capital expenditure, and use the company's reconciled adjusted net income for the cash-conversion test. Define operating return on assets as **full-year filed GAAP operating income / the same year-end's total assets**, retaining goodwill and cash: this deliberately tests all capital tied up, not only selected factory assets. It is **pre-tax operating ROA, not ROIC**. A disclosed material impairment of the expanded production assets prompts immediate review rather than waiting for the annual ratios. If accounts are delayed, review that delay explicitly; never manufacture a threshold result.

proposals.warning: At the **29 October 2026** Q3 release, re-read if total variable fees per million fall **more than 10% year on year**, or cash-credit fees per million fall **more than 15%**, independently of total revenue growth. Q2 baselines are $2.14 and $114.03, down 7.2% and 11.4%. These are my deterioration thresholds, not management guidance. Also review any two consecutive monthly declines in Tradeweb's fully electronic US high-grade or high-yield share versus the corresponding prior-year months.
proposals.break: By **28 February 2027**, exit the proposed share under §5.1 if either fee measure breaches its warning threshold in **both Q3 and Q4**, even if ADV, market share and total revenue rise. Persistent fee erosion itself invalidates the expected economics; it is not conditional on also losing market share. Missing comparable data triggers review, never an automatic pass. Changes in product mix are investigated at warning and do not silently erase the precommitted break. Fee definitions and baselines: [Q2 10-Q, pp. 54–57](https://investors.tradeweb.com/static-files/2f970380-b2c2-4f2e-8a86-cfe3eba32d70). Results date: [issuer announcement](https://investors.tradeweb.com/news-releases/news-release-details/tradeweb-announces-date-third-quarter-2026-financial-results). February is my assessment deadline, not an announced Q4 date.

proposals.warning: At each monthly review, trigger a re-read if Netflix's share of US TV viewing in **Nielsen's The Gauge** is at least **5% lower relative to the same month a year earlier in two consecutive published months**, irrespective of revenue or margin. Also warn if Netflix discloses falling total global view hours at its next annual engagement release. These are my thresholds, not company guidance. Revenue growing while audience share falls does not clear the warning.
proposals.break: By **28 February 2027**, exit these proposed shares under §5.1 if the comparable Nielsen share is **at least 10% lower year on year for three consecutive published months**. This is a direct sustained-loss-of-attention test and requires neither a revenue miss nor lower margins. It can fire sooner if the three observations arrive earlier. Monthly seasonality is handled with same-month comparisons, not a June-to-July comparison. Use [Nielsen's monthly source](https://www.nielsen.com/data-center/the-gauge/) and its underlying releases. The latest retrieved release covers **June**, published **18 August**; it is not September audience data. Nielsen flags methodology changes this autumn: use comparable or restated observations, and escalate an unavailable comparison for review rather than count it as a pass. This US-TV proxy misses phones and international audiences, so it cannot fully falsify global competitive risk. The separate operating check is the next Q3 result: compare reported operating margin with the **33.2%** company forecast. A miss prompts review, but cannot replace the audience test. [Company forecast and engagement cadence](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/FINAL-Q2-26-Shareholder-Letter.pdf).

proposals.warning: At FY2026 results, locally estimated for **5 November 2026**, re-read if consolidated physical volumes decline again year on year, **or** GAAP operating margin is below **19%**, **or** full-year free cash flow does not exceed **70% of adjusted net income**. Any one is sufficient. The volume statement may be directional, as in the current filing; an omitted bridge is unavailable evidence, not stable volumes. The cash reference is management's commitment; 19% is my early-warning threshold.
proposals.break: For these **additional shares**, exit under §5.1 if GAAP operating margin is below **18% in each of two successive post-entry quarters**, assessed by **28 February 2027**, regardless of sales growth. This standalone margin test addresses the Review's concern that price-led growth could keep a combined margin-and-growth test green. Also break if management discloses a material permanent shutdown or impairment of the capacity on which the efficiency case depends; ordinary restructuring expense alone is not that event. Use filed operating profit **after** reorganisation charges. The new margin-only test can fire while price rises keep revenue growing. It does not retrospectively change the conditions Leo accepted on the original three shares in [the 8 September proposal](2026-09-08-2133-MWA.md); the Review must distinguish the original holding and this proposed top-up until Leo adopts a common rule. [Current quarter filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1350593/000135059326000036/mwa-20260630.htm), [cash-conversion commitment](https://ir.muellerwaterproducts.com/press-releases/2026/08-05-2026-211118748).

proposals.warning: At each new monthly Nielsen US Gauge release through **31 March 2027**, Netflix's share of total television usage **below 7.5% in two consecutive comparable months** triggers a re-read. The independently verified May 2026 baseline is **8.0%**; this threshold represents a sustained half-point loss, not a company target. It tests attention directly even if price increases keep revenue growing. The [May report](https://content.nielsen.com/gauge-and-glossary) supplies the baseline; the [June report](https://www.nielsen.com/news-center/2026/fox-and-nbcuniversal-score-with-fifa-world-cup-2026-success-in-nielsens-june-gauge-reports/) shows why one sports-heavy month is insufficient.
proposals.break: By **31 March 2027**, three consecutive comparable monthly releases below **7.0%** break this proposal's assumption of a sufficiently durable audience franchise and call for exit under §5.1, even if headline revenue meets guidance. This is my risk threshold, not a statistical claim that US TV measures all Netflix use. Do not join observations across a Nielsen methodology change without a comparable back series: obtain the restatement or record the metric as unavailable and re-review the position. An unavailable series is not a green result. Quarterly revenue and operating margin are secondary checks, not substitutes for this attention test. No automatic exit is inferred from one weak title or a share-price fall.
